arxiv-2206-08680.title: BITS Pilani at HinglishEval: Quality Evaluation for Code-Mixed Hinglish Text Using Transformers
arxiv-2206-08680.creator: Shaz Furniturewala, Vijay Kumari, Amulya Ratna Dash, Hriday Kedia
arxiv-2206-08680.description: Abstract Code-Mixed text data consists of sentences having words or phrases from more than one language. Most multi-lingual communities worldwide communicate using multiple languages, with English usually one of them. Hinglish is a Code-Mixed text composed of Hindi and English but written in Roman script.

arxiv-2206-09016.title: Path-Gradient Estimators for Continuous Normalizing Flows
arxiv-2206-09016.creator: Lorenz Vaitl, Kim A. Nicoli, Shinichi Nakajima, Pan Kessel
arxiv-2206-09016.description: Abstract Recent work has established a path-gradient estimator for simple variational Gaussian distributions and has argued that the path-gradient is particularly beneficial in the regime in which the variational distribution approaches the exact target distribution. In many applications, this regime can however not be reached by a simple Gaussian variational distribution.

arxiv-2210-05750.title: High-power laser beam shaping using a metasurface for shock excitation and focusing at the microscale
arxiv-2210-05750.creator: Yun Kai, Jet Lem, Marcus Ossiander, Maryna L. Meretska, Vyacheslav Sokurenko, Steven E. Kooi, Federico Capasso, Keith A. Nelson, Thomas Pezeril
arxiv-2210-05750.description: Abstract Achieving high repeatability and efficiency in laser-induced strong shock wave excitation remains a significant technical challenge, as evidenced by the extensive efforts undertaken at large-scale national laboratories to optimize the compression of light element pellets. In this study, we propose and model a novel optical design for generating strong shocks at a tabletop scale.

arxiv-2312-08462.title: Fracton models from product codes
arxiv-2312-08462.creator: Yi Tan, Brenden Roberts, Nathanan Tantivasadakarn, Beni Yoshida, Norman Y. Yao
arxiv-2312-08462.description: Abstract We explore a deep connection between fracton order and product codes. In particular, we propose and analyze conditions on classical seed codes which lead to fracton order in the resulting quantum product codes. Depending on the properties of the input codes, product codes can realize either Type-I or Type-II fracton models, in both nonlocal and local constructions.

arxiv-2404-09391.title: Privacy at a Price: Exploring its Dual Impact on AI Fairness Journal: Publication Name
arxiv-2404-09391.creator: Mengmeng Yang, Ming Ding, Youyang Qu, Wei Ni, David Smith, Thierry Rakotoarivelo
arxiv-2404-09391.description: Abstract The potential of machine learning raises significant challenges regarding privacy and fairness. While Differential Privacy (DP) safeguards privacy, it can unevenly affect prediction accuracy among demographic groups. Our study reveals that while DP initially increases accuracy disparity, it diminishes at higher privacy levels. Gradient clipping curbs DP’s negative impact on fairness. Keywords—Privacy-preserving, fairness, differential privacy.

arxiv-2410-11753.title: Identification and modelling of optically thin inverse Compton scattering in the prompt emission of GRB131014A
arxiv-2410-11753.creator: Pragyan Pratim Bordoloi, Shabnam Iyyani
arxiv-2410-11753.description: Abstract The mechanism responsible for the prompt gamma-ray emission of a gamma-ray burst continues to remain an enigma. The detailed analysis of the spectrum of GRB 131014A observed by the Fermi gamma ray burst monitor and Large Area Telescope has revealed an unconventional spectral shape that significantly deviates from the typical Band function.

arxiv-2502-13672.title: Atmospheric boundary layer over urban roughness: validation of large-eddy simulation
arxiv-2502-13672.creator: Ming Teng (滕明), Josep M. Duró Diaz, Ernest Mestres, Jordi Muela Castro, Oriol Lehmkuhl, Ivette Rodriguez
arxiv-2502-13672.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Ming Teng (滕明), Josep M. Duró Diaz, Ernest Mestres, Jordi Muela Castro, Oriol Lehmkuhl, Ivette Rodriguez. The study presents wall-modeled large-eddy simulations (LES) characterizing the flow features of a neutral atmospheric boundary layer over two urban-like roughness geometries: an array of three-dimensional square prisms and the ‘Michel-Stadt’ geometry model. The former is an arrangement of idealized building blocks and incorporates a 7 × 7 7\times 7 array of wall-mounted prisms with identical spacing ratios in both transversal and longitudinal directions.

arxiv-2510-25492.title: Cubic polynomials and sums of two squares
arxiv-2510-25492.creator: Siddharth Iyer
arxiv-2510-25492.description: Abstract . We state a lower bound for how often an irreducible monic cubic polynomial is a sum of two squares ( □ 2 \raisebox{-2.15277pt}{\scalebox{2}{$\square$}}_{2} ). To do so, we rely on a two-dimensional unit argument, and degree six number fields.

arxiv-2511-22247.title: FIGROTD: A Friendly-to-Handle Dataset for Image Guided Retrieval with Optional Text
arxiv-2511-22247.creator: Hoang-Bao Le, Allie Tran, Binh T. Nguyen, Liting Zhou, Cathal Gurrin
arxiv-2511-22247.description: Abstract Image-Guided Retrieval with Optional Text (IGROT) unifies visual retrieval (without text) and composed retrieval (with text). Despite its relevance in applications like Google Image and Bing, progress has been limited by the lack of an accessible benchmark and methods that balance performance across subtasks.

britannica-1911-minto-william.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-minto-william.description: Article 'Minto, William' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 18), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. was born at Auchintoul, Aberdeenshire, on the 10th of October 1845. He was educated at Aberdeen University, and spent a year at Merton College, Oxford. He was assistant professor under Alexander Bain at Aberdeen for some years; from 1874 to 1878 he edited the Examiner, and in 1880 he was made full professor of logic and English at Aberdeen.

pmc-10541936.title: Scoping Review of Restorative Justice in Academics and Medicine: A Powerful Tool for Justice Equity Diversity and Inclusion
pmc-10541936.creator: Gregory Sawin, Christopher L. Klasson, Samantha Kaplan, Jennifer Larson Sawin, Ann Brown, Sonoo Thadaney Israni, Jessica Schonberg, Ada Gregory
pmc-10541936.description: Purpose:Restorative Justice (RJ) as a practice and mindset is growing within academic medicine and health care. The authors aim to categorize the extent to which RJ training and practices have been researched, explored, and applied within health care, medicine, and academic contexts.

pmc-10712101.title: GBDT_KgluSite: An improved computational prediction model for lysine glutarylation sites based on feature fusion and GBDT classifier
pmc-10712101.creator: Xin Liu, Bao Zhu, Xia-Wei Dai, Zhi-Ao Xu, Rui Li, Yuting Qian, Ya-Ping Lu, Wenqing Zhang, Yong Liu, Junnian Zheng
pmc-10712101.description: BackgroundLysine glutarylation (Kglu) is one of the most important Post-translational modifications (PTMs), which plays significant roles in various cellular functions, including metabolism, mitochondrial processes, and translation. Therefore, accurate identification of the Kglu site is important for elucidating protein molecular function.

pmc-11384064.title: Prediction of Glioma enhancement pattern using a MRI radiomics-based model
pmc-11384064.creator: Wen Wang, Yu Wang, WenYi Meng, ErJia Guo, HuiShan He, GuangLong Huang, WenLe He, YuanKui Wu
pmc-11384064.description: Contrast-MRI scans carry risks associated with the chemical contrast agents. Accurate prediction of enhancement pattern of gliomas has potential in avoiding contrast agent administration to patients. This study aimed to develop a machine learning radiomics model that can accurately predict enhancement pattern of gliomas based on T2 fluid attenuated inversion recovery images.

pmc-11620241.title: Process standardization and characterization of Mies: Ethiopian honey wine
pmc-11620241.creator: Weleba Muesho Gebremichael, Kiros Hagos Abay, Desta Berhe Sbhatu, Goitom Gebreyohannes Berhe, Gebreselema Gebreyohannes
pmc-11620241.description: Mies is a delicious honey wine traditionally processed in Ethiopia and Eritrea. This study aimed to investigate the standardization and characterization of high-quality Mies. The ingredients for Mies preparation were collected, and three formulations were created by varying the amounts of Gesho and honey.

pmc-12563318.title: Diet-Driven Variations in Longevity and Fecundity of the Endangered Tiger Beetle Cicindela anchoralis (Coleoptera: Carabidae)
pmc-12563318.creator: Deokjea Cha, Anya Lim, Jong-Kook Jung, Rafał Gosik
pmc-12563318.description: Simple SummaryWe studied how prey type affects reproduction and lifespan in the endangered tiger beetle Cicindela anchoralis. Tiger beetles fed on crickets (high-P:C) produced more eggs but lived shorter, while those fed on ants (low-P:C) lived longer but reproduced less. Despite this trade-off, beetles of both sexes preferred crickets. This indicates a life-history strategy prioritizing reproduction over longevity.

pmc-12737270.title: Wireless Ultra-Low-Power Sensor Platform for Environmental Monitoring
pmc-12737270.creator: Jannis Winnefeld, Metin Kizilarslan, Werner Knop, Jens Passoke, Jeongyeup Paek
pmc-12737270.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). This paper presents an open, modular sensor platform based on wireless energy and data transmission. The platform is powered by the carrier signal of a transceiver and transmits the measured sensor data using backscatter modulation. Through the use of modular ready-to-buy components, the sensor platform can be flexibly adapted to different applications and is therefore suitable for both building automation systems and industrial automation tasks.

pmc-13547515.title: Target-level convergence of directional prefrontal connectivity across Alzheimer’s disease stages: an fNIRS study
pmc-13547515.creator: Nida Mateen, Rana Muhammad Kaleem Ullah, Jisoo Baik, Keum-Shik Hong, Min-Kyoung Kang, Chang-Seok Kim, Yong-Il Shin
pmc-13547515.description: BackgroundAlzheimer’s disease (AD) is increasingly recognized as involving network-level dysfunction rather than isolated regional impairment. Although functional and effective connectivity have been studied in dementia, the reorganization of directional information flow within prefrontal networks remains incompletely characterized, particularly with functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS).
